alex.chen: FYI saw a burst of AWS KMS throttle errors in prod around 14:02 UTC. ~4% decrypt failures, tail latency up to 2s.
maria.gupta: Thanks — which key/region? any request ID?
alex.chen: Key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd... , region us-west-2. Logs attached by sec-bot below. No deploy at the time.
sec-bot: [log snippet] 
ERROR KMS Throttling: ThrottlingException, requestId=7f3a2c, status=429, attempt=1
Stack: kms.Decrypt -> envelope.decrypt -> storage.write
sanjay: Could be a thundering herd: we pushed a worker pool scale yesterday that increased parallel decrypts. Any RBAC changes recently?
dave.h: I rolled out the feature to prewarm model shards but shouldn't touch crypto paths. IAM policy for the service principal unchanged.
maria.gupta: Ok. Temporary mitigation idea: increase client SDK retry with jitter + short DEK cache on hosts (safely bounded TTL). Also add a circuit breaker so we don't flood KMS.
alex.chen: Agreed. We've already enabled local DEK cache (ttl=300s) for request paths and bumped retry to 6 attempts with exponential backoff. Early numbers look promising: throttle errors down to ~0.2%.
sanjay: Can you paste the retry config we used?
alex.chen: Sure:
```
kms_client:
  max_attempts: 6
  base_backoff_ms: 100
  backoff_multiplier: 2.0
  jitter: full
  max_backoff_ms: 2000
```
maria.gupta: Also enabled a client-side token bucket limiter (20 QPS per instance) to smooth bursts to KMS. That prevented further bursts on the next wave.
dave.h: What about audit logging? We should flag any increase in KMS 429s as a security/compliance event (audit trail + ticket).
sec-bot: Created alert rule ENG-SEC-KMS-THROTTLE (threshold: 0.5% 5m) and ticket INC-184123. Audit entry exported to long-term logs with tag kms_throttle:true.
alex.chen: Noted. One more root-cause suspicion: we found a background job that wasn't using envelope cache and retried aggressively on error; it multiplied calls. I opened a PR to adopt shared DEK cache.
maria.gupta: Good catch. Action items: 1) Make DEK cache default for background jobs (PR already referenced). 2) Add per-key concurrency limiter in our KMS client. 3) Update runbook for KMS throttling with safe fallbacks (cache-first, circuit-breaker, alerting).
sanjay: For runbook language, be explicit about what fallbacks are allowed under compliance: cached DEKs with TTL <= 5m and always log key usage. No silent local-only encryption.
dave.h: Also add a check in deployment e2e to ensure workers don't spike parallel decrypts beyond per-instance limit.
ops-bot: Rollback bot: no rollbacks triggered. No ongoing incident.
maria.gupta: We'll schedule a short post-incident review tomorrow. For now, monitoring shows latency back to normal. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
alex.chen: I'll follow up with a short summary for compliance with the timeline and mitigations.
sanjay: Please include IAM policy diff check in the postmortem so we can rule out accidental perms changes.
maria.gupta: Will do. Closing thread when PR merges and runbook is updated.
